scope: Native declaration placement and typed text ordering. Incremental work in the unfinished C# renderer objective.

implementation.declarations: Find the direct defs region independently of markup position, then remove that exact declaration node before checking the single markup root. Existing duplicate-region rejection remains.
implementation.orderedText: Accept compatible string/keyword operands and compare with native string.CompareOrdinal. Preserve numeric comparisons, invalid/absent propagation and compile-time rejection of statically disjoint operands.
implementation.platform: Existing native DOM and ordinal UTF-16 comparison. No new dependency or browser runtime layer.

declarationPlacement.coverage: Default and supplied prop values flow through a computed declaration with defs before or after the markup root.

orderedText.coverage: All ordered operators, equality boundaries, ISO month limits, numeric-looking strings, case and surrogate-pair ordering, current inputs, null and statically disjoint numeric/text operands.

catalogCharacterization.meaning: Per-entry compilation with declared source dependencies. This is not full catalog rendering or behavior qualification.
resolvedFirstFailures: Column now reaches its keyed style rather than rejecting declaration placement.
Calendar and its picker consumers now reach format calls rather than rejecting text comparisons.
catalogCharacterization.dependencyLimit: The standalone Data Table entry needs its accepted Column definition in the compilation graph. Its unknown-component failure is an audit-context limitation until reproduced with that definition supplied.

review.mode: One bounded inline correctness and simplification pass, current session model. No agents or cross-model review.

limits: Keyed styles and Intl formatting remain unfinished.
Complete native application, forms, hydration and catalog behavior qualification remain unfinished.
Full matched latency, throughput, retained/peak memory and serving qualification remain unfinished.
Native package remains private and unpublished.
